title: Exact module lower shriek under local slice equivalences
statement: Work in the small-site universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous and cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1). Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal D$ and put $R'=R\circ u$, with the identity structural ring map. For module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $T:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R')$ be precomposition. Suppose that for every $U\in\mathcal C$ the induced functor $u_U:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal D/u(U)$, $(V\to U)\mapsto(u(V)\to u(U))$, is an equivalence of sites and identifies their restricted ring sheaves [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Suppose also that fibre products and equalizers exist in $\mathcal C$ and are preserved by $u$, where an equalizer of $r,s:X\to Y$ is the universal arrow $e:E\to X$ with $re=se$. Then $T$ has an additive left adjoint $L:\operatorname{Mod}(R')\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ which is exact. If $L^{\mathrm{Ab}}$ denotes the left adjoint of precomposition on abelian sheaves, there is a natural isomorphism $\mathrm{forget}\circ L\simeq L^{\mathrm{Ab}}\circ\mathrm{forget}$, where $\mathrm{forget}$ drops the ring action. No terminal object of either site is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0797 (lemma-lower-shriek-modules), 0798 (remark-when-shriek-equal), and 04BH (lemma-exactness-lower-shriek). The equivalence on slices makes the comparison (equation-compare-on-localizations) of 0798 an isomorphism.

proof.text: The module categories are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-trf-ringed-site-restriction-generator-data] to $u,R$: $T$ is additive, and its small-sum class $\mathcal P$ epimorphically generates $\operatorname{Mod}(R')$. For $P=\bigoplus_iE_{U_i}^{R'}$, the displayed natural bijections in that statement corepresent $N\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}(P,TN)$ by $\bigoplus_iE_{uU_i}^{R}$. An isomorphism of $P$ with such a sum gives the same corepresentation by precomposing Hom with that isomorphism. Thus [lem-trf-partially-defined-module-adjoint], with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(R')$, supplies $L\dashv T$. All sums are small by the generator statement.

source.place: Tag 0797, lemma-lower-shriek-modules: its evaluation bijections and the epimorphic-generator adjoint criterion (Homology Tag 0793).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], $L$ preserves finite colimits. Apply [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive] to the abelian module categories of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: $L$ is additive. Fix its adjunction unit $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 0797, the additive module adjunction; elementary consequences of the adjunction.

proof.text: Precomposition on abelian sheaves has a left adjoint $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf] and [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. The same applies to each $u_U$, giving $A_U\dashv T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}$. Indeed the localized coverings are underlying coverings by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; continuity and covering pullback preservation restrict from $u$, and cocontinuity lifts a cover of $u(V)$ to a cover of $V$, keeping the composite maps to $U$. The sites and their comma categories remain small. Write $R_U=R|_{u(U)}$; restriction gives $R^{\prime}|_U=T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}R_U$ section by section.

source.place: Tag 0798, localized square; sites.tex lemma-localize-cocontinuous; abelian adjunction as in lemma-g-shriek-adjoint.

proof.text: Fix $U$. A quasi-inverse to the site equivalence $u_U$ preserves covers, so precomposition with it sends sheaves to sheaves: its sheaf-condition diagrams identify with those on the corresponding covers. The two quasi-inverse isomorphisms then give inverse functors on abelian sheaves, with their group laws unchanged. Thus $T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}$ is fully faithful. Its adjunction counit $c_U:A_UT_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}R_U\to R_U$ is invertible: fullness lifts the unit $\eta^{U}_{T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}R_U}$ to $d:R_U\to A_UT_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}R_U$. The triangle identity and faithfulness give $c_Ud=1$. Both $dc_U$ and $1$ have adjunct $\eta^{U}_{T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}R_U}$, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $dc_U=1$. This works for every $U$ without a terminal object in either original site.

source.place: Tag 0798, equation-compare-on-localizations; elementary verification of its hypothesis using the given site equivalences and the adjunction identities.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-module-shriek-forgetful-counit-criterion] to $L,A,A_U$. Step 4 verifies precisely its counit hypotheses on the restricted ring sheaves, so its specified natural map $\gamma:A F_{\mathcal C}\to F_{\mathcal D}L$ is invertible. Its inverse is the required natural isomorphism $\mathrm{forget}\circ L\simeq L^{\mathrm{Ab}}\circ\mathrm{forget}$, with $L^{\mathrm{Ab}}=A$. Exactness will follow in Step 6.

Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-lower-shriek-exact] to $u$ and the abelian left adjoint $A$ from Step 3. Its hypotheses are exactly the given continuity, cocontinuity, fibre products, equalizers and their preservation, so $A$ is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], forgetting module actions is faithful and preserves kernels and cokernels on both small sites. Hence an input short exact module sequence becomes short exact after forgetting and applying $A$; the natural isomorphism of Step 5 identifies it with the underlying sequence of its image under $L$. This implies module exactness: its kernel, cokernel and middle homology have zero underlying abelian sheaves, since forgetting preserves kernels and cokernels; faithfulness then makes their identity maps zero, so these objects are zero. Thus $L$ is exact, completing all clauses.
